title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe EDGX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Introduce a Trade by Trade Report for EDGX Options and To Amend Its Fee Schedule To Adopt Fees for the Trade by Trade Report
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe EDGX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Introduce a Trade by Trade Report for EDGX Options and To Amend Its Fee Schedule To Adopt Fees for the Trade by Trade Report

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to introduce a Trade by Trade report (``TBT Report'') for its equity options platform (``EDGX Options''), which will be available for purchase by Options Members and non-Options Members, and to amend the EDGX Options fee schedule to adopt fees for the TBT Report, including a free sample. The proposed TBT Report is based on the TBT Report recently adopted by the Exchange's affiliated options exchange, Cboe Exchange, Inc. (``Cboe Options''). Trade by Trade Report The TBT Report will provide subscribers with comprehensive trade- by-trade level detail for each options transaction executed on EDGX Options. The TBT Report will be produced and updated at the end of each trading day and be made available to subscribers overnight after midnight Eastern Time (i.e., T+1), ensuring that the data is strictly historical and cannot be used to influence intraday trading decisions. Specifically, each row in the TBT Report will represent a single trade event and will include transaction time, underlying symbol, Options Symbology Initiative (``OSI'') details (e.g., root, expiry, strike, call/put), trade size, trade price, market context indicators (e.g., National Best Bid/National Best Offer, EDGX Options best bid/ best offer), side of the market (i.e., buy or sell), transaction type (opening or closing), and origin (i.e., the Capacity of the order, such as Priority Customer, Professional, broker-dealer, and Market Maker), as well as, for a subscriber that is an Options Member, that Options Member's execution IDs for both Simple Book and Complex Order Book trades, which will better allow for accurate linkage and reconstruction of trading activity. The Exchange anticipates a wide variety of market participants would purchase the TBT Report, including, but not limited to, individual customers, buy-side investors, and investment banks. The Exchange believes the proposed TBT Report will aid subscribers in performing detailed transaction-level analysis, compliance checks, and historical market reconstruction. The TBT Report may also serve as a foundation for analytics on liquidity, price formation, and trade behavior at a trade-by-trade level. The proposed TBT Report is a completely voluntary product, in that the Exchange is not required by any rule or regulation to make this data available, and potential subscribers are not required to purchase the TBT Report and may do so only if they voluntarily choose to. Proposed Fees The Exchange proposes to provide in the EDGX Options fee schedule that firms may purchase the TBT Report on a subscription basis or by ad hoc request for a specified month. The Exchange proposes to assess a monthly fee of $6,000 for subscribing to the TBT Report. The Exchange also proposes to adopt a fee of $4,000 per month for ad hoc requests of the TBT Report. An ad hoc request can be for any number of months for which the data is available, beginning with March 1, 2019. The Exchange also proposes to offer a free sample consisting of End-of-Day Trade by Trade Historical Data for the period July 1, 2022 through July 31, 2022. The free sample will be available to both Options Members and non-Options Members who have not previously purchased the TBT Report or previously received a free sample. The Exchange believes the proposed free sample will serve as an incentive for new subscribers to start purchasing such data. Particularly, the Exchange believes it will give potential subscribers the ability to evaluate historical options trading data before purchasing the TBT Report. The Exchange notes that Cboe Options is concurrently filing a proposed rule change to adopt the same free sample for its TBT Report. The Exchange also notes that another exchange offers a free trial for new subscribers of a similar data product. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act. Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5) requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5) requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange also believes the proposed fees are consistent with Section 6(b)(4) of the Act, which requires that the rules of an exchange provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its members and issuers and other persons using its facilities. In adopting Regulation NMS, the Commission granted self-regulatory organizations (``SROs'') and broker-dealers increased authority and flexibility to offer new and unique market data to the public. It was believed that this authority would expand the amount of data available to consumers, and also spur innovation and competition for the provision of market data. The Exchange believes that the proposed TBT Report would further broaden the availability of U.S. options market data to investors consistent with the principles of Regulation NMS. The proposal also promotes increased transparency through the dissemination of the TBT Report. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act. Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5) requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5) requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange also believes the proposed fees are consistent with Section 6(b)(4) of the Act, which requires that the rules of an exchange provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its members and issuers and other persons using its facilities. In adopting Regulation NMS, the Commission granted self-regulatory organizations (``SROs'') and broker-dealers increased authority and flexibility to offer new and unique market data to the public. It was believed that this authority would expand the amount of data available to consumers, and also spur innovation and competition for the provision of market data. The Exchange believes that the proposed TBT Report would further broaden the availability of U.S. options market data to investors consistent with the principles of Regulation NMS. title: Amended D-Peg On-Entry Behavior During Active Signal Period
raw_text:
Amended D-Peg On-Entry Behavior During Active Signal Period
Category: Trading; Alert 2026-042
Overview Effective Tuesday, November 17, 2026, IEX Equities will extend Crumbling Quote Indicator (CQI) and Quote Imbalance Indicator (QII) protections to on-entry behavior for Discretionary Peg (D-Peg) orders. When the CQI or QII, as selected by the User, is active (i.e., it is “on”) for the order’s side of the market, an incoming D-Peg will post at its resting price instead of seeking an execution at the less aggressive of the Midpoint Price or its limit price. Details The change applies to D-Peg orders with a time-in-force of DAY, GTX, SYS, or GTT. During the applicable signal period (i.e., when the CQI or QII is on), these orders will be priced and ranked at the less aggressive of: One minimum price variant (MPV) below the NBB for buys, or above the NBO for sells; or The order’s limit price, if any. D-Peg orders will also no longer execute on entry in locked or crossed markets while the applicable indicator is on. Behavior of IOC/FOK orders or when the CQI and QII are off is unaffected and remains unchanged. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change to Set Fees for Nasdaq TotalView Plus and Nasdaq Basic Plus
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change to Set Fees for Nasdaq TotalView Plus and Nasdaq Basic Plus

1. Purpose The purpose of the proposed rule change is to set fees for Nasdaq TotalView Plus and Nasdaq Basic Plus at or below the fees currently charged for the combined underlying Depth-of-Book and Top-of-Book products offered by the Nasdaq U.S. Equity Markets. The proposed fees will provide customers with the option of lowering market data, networking, and connectivity costs by replacing three separate feeds with one, and setting fees for these two new consolidated data products at a level that is at or below current market data fees for the combined underlying products. The Exchange believes that this proposal will facilitate the transition to overnight trading in December 2026. As discussed in the product filing for Nasdaq TotalView Plus and Nasdaq Basic Plus, liquidity may be limited for certain stocks in the overnight session. The two new consolidated data products will address this issue by providing investors with a broader view of the market than any of the individual underlying individual exchange feeds, thereby improving the ability of investors to analyze trading in a lower liquidity environment. Nasdaq TotalView Plus Nasdaq TotalView Plus includes, with respect to stocks listed on Nasdaq or on any exchange other than Nasdaq, all orders and quotes from all members of any of the Nasdaq U.S. Equity Markets and displayed on a Nasdaq U.S. Equity Market, including all information currently disseminated through Nasdaq TotalView, Nasdaq Texas TotalView, and PSX TotalView, and the aggregate size of such orders and quotes at each price level in the execution functionality of the Nasdaq U.S. equity markets. Nasdaq Basic Plus Nasdaq Basic Plus offers the best bid and offer and last sale information for stocks listed on any of the Nasdaq U.S. Equity Markets or any exchange other than Nasdaq and displayed on any of the Nasdaq U.S. Equity Markets or the FINRA/Nasdaq TRF, including all information currently disseminated through Nasdaq Basic, Nasdaq Texas BBO feeds, Nasdaq Texas Last Sale, PSX BBO Feeds, and PSX Last Sale. Proposed Fees As set forth in detail below, Nasdaq proposes to set fees for Nasdaq TotalView Plus and Nasdaq Basic Plus at or below fees currently charged for the Depth-of-Book and Top-of-Book products offered by the Nasdaq U.S. Equity Markets. This, together with the networking and connectivity savings inherent in lowering the number of data feeds, is designed to maximize the distribution of consolidated data feeds to investors throughout the 23 hour, 5 days per week schedule set to begin in December 2026. The Exchange proposes to offer Nasdaq TotalView Plus for the same Professional and Non-Professional Subscriber and enterprise license fees as Nasdaq TotalView. To ensure that market data vendors will be able to offer competing consolidated data products, any firm that certifies to Nasdaq that it will consolidate Nasdaq TotalView, Nasdaq Texas TotalView and Nasdaq PSX TotalView into a data feed solely for external redistribution shall be exempt from Nasdaq Texas Market Data Distributor Fees and Nasdaq PSX Market Data Distributor Fees, and the Monthly External Distributor Fees at Equity 7, Section 119(b) shall be reduced by $350 per month. These three discounts will ensure that vendors will be able to cover the cost of consolidating the underlying feeds. The Exchange proposes to offer Nasdaq Basic Plus for the same Professional and Non-Professional Subscriber, enterprise license, and Distributor fees as Nasdaq Basic. To ensure that other market data vendors will be able to offer competing consolidated data products, Nasdaq proposes to charge the same monthly administrative and data consolidation fees for Nasdaq Basic Plus as are currently charged for Nasdaq Last Sale Plus to both Internal Distributors and External Distributors to cover the costs of data feed consolidation to be incurred by market data vendors. With respect to the Market Data Enterprise License for Display Usage, which currently offers both Nasdaq TotalView and Nasdaq Basic in the same enterprise license, the Exchange proposes to offer the Nasdaq TotalView Plus and Nasdaq Basic Plus feeds for the same fees currently charged for the Nasdaq TotalView and Nasdaq Basic. Details for each of the proposed fees follow. TotalView Plus Subscriber Fees Nasdaq proposes to offer Nasdaq TotalView Plus for the same Professional and Non-Professional Subscriber fees as Nasdaq TotalView. This is, in effect, a waiver of Subscriber and Non-Display Usage fees for Texas TotalView and Entitlement fees for Nasdaq PSX TotalView. Current Professional Subscriber fees for Nasdaq TotalView are $84 per month (operative January 1, 2026). Non-Display Usage fees based upon Direct Access depend on the number of Subscribers: $412 per month for 1-39 Subscribers (operative January 1, 2026); $16,490 per month for 40-99 Subscribers (operative January 1, 2026); $32,990 per month for 100-249 Subscribers (operative January 1, 2026); and $75,000.00 per month per firm for over 250 Subscribers. Non-Professional Subscriber fees for Nasdaq TotalView are $15 per month. All of these Professional and Non-Professional Subscriber fees and Non-Display Usage fees will be the same for both Nasdaq TotalView and Nasdaq TotalView Plus. Enterprise License Fees Nasdaq offers two monthly enterprise licenses for Nasdaq TotalView, one for $25,000, and another for $500,000. The $25,000 per month enterprise license offers customers the right to provide Nasdaq TotalView for Display Usage for Internal Distribution, or for External Distribution to both Professional and Non-Professional Subscribers with whom the firm has a brokerage relationship. Purchasers of this license also pay a monthly fee of $9 for each Non-Professional Subscriber and a monthly fee of $60 for each Professional Subscriber for Display Usage based upon Direct or Indirect Access. These three discounts will ensure that vendors will be able to cover the cost of consolidating the underlying fees. Nasdaq will offer Nasdaq Basic Plus for the same Professional and Non-Professional Subscriber, enterprise license, and Distributor fees as Nasdaq Basic. To ensure that other market data vendors will be able to offer competing consolidated data products, Nasdaq proposes to charge the same monthly administrative and data consolidation fees for Nasdaq Basic Plus as are currently charged for Nasdaq Last Sale Plus to both Internal Distributors and External Distributors to cover the costs of data feed consolidation to be incurred by market data vendors. Vendors would be able to apply this fee reduction, together with the waiver of Nasdaq Texas Market Data Distributor Fees, and the $350 per month reduction in Monthly External Distributor Fees for the Nasdaq Stock Market, to cover the cost of forming their own consolidated feed, thereby allowing vendors to compete with Nasdaq in the sale of consolidated data products using the depth of book data from Nasdaq affiliates. This is to ensure that Nasdaq can offer Nasdaq TotalView Plus for the same Subscriber fees as Nasdaq TotalView. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; BOX Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Adopt Rules To Govern the Trading of FLEX Equity Options in Electronic Auctions
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; BOX Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Adopt Rules To Govern the Trading of FLEX Equity Options in Electronic Auctions

1. Purpose FLEX Equity Options are customized options contracts that allow investors to tailor contract terms for exchange-listed equity options. FLEX Equity Options are designed to meet the needs of investors for greater flexibility in selecting the terms of options within the parameters of the Exchange's rules. FLEX Equity Options are not preestablished for trading and are not listed individually for trading on BOX. Rather, investors select FLEX Equity Option terms and are limited by the parameters set forth in Rule 5055 in their selection of those terms. As a result, FLEX Equity Options allow investors to specify more specific, individualized investment objectives than may be available to them in the standardized options market. FLEX Equity Options and FLEX Open Outcry (``FOO'') Orders were approved for trading on BOX on May 15, 2024. FOO Orders are limited solely to the BOX Trading Floor. The Exchange now proposes to adopt rules that will govern the listing and trading of FLEX Equity Options on the Exchange's electronic market. The Exchange notes that FLEX options trade electronically on Cboe Exchange, Inc. (``CBOE''), Nasdaq PHLX LLC (``Nasdaq PHLX''), and Nasdaq ISE, LLC (``Nasdaq ISE''). The proposal allows for the trading of FLEX Equity Options in electronic auctions in a substantially similar manner as both CBOE and Nasdaq ISE's electronic markets, with certain intended differences primarily to align to current System behavior (and especially current auction behavior) to provide increased consistency for Participants trading FLEX Equity Options and Non-FLEX Equity Options on BOX, as discussed in detail below. The Exchange notes further that in Nasdaq ISE's recently approved filing to adopt FLEX options and electronic FLEX options trading, Nasdaq ISE compared its proposed rules to CBOE's established rules. This proposal will also compare the Exchange's proposed rules to CBOE's established rules. Accordingly, the Exchange has omitted certain CBOE rules from the proposed rules due to differences in scope and operation of FLEX trading at CBOE compared to the proposed scope and operation of FLEX trading on BOX, each as noted below. For example, the Exchange proposes only to add price improvement and solicitation auctions and will not add Electronic FLEX Auctions as defined in CBOE Rule 5.72(c). Further, BOX does not allow prices in FLEX trading to be expressed as percentages. The Exchange proposes amendments to Rule 5055 to accommodate FLEX Equity Option trading in electronic auctions. Specifically, the Exchange proposes to include Rules 7155 (FLEX PIP) and 7275 (FLEX Solicitation Auction) as Rules that govern FLEX Equity Options trading, in proposed Rule 5055(a), along with current Rule 7605 (FOO Orders). The Exchange also proposes to remove the language from Rule 5055(b)(3), which provides that FLEX Equity Options may not be traded using any other order type than FOO Orders or other trading mechanism offered by the Exchange and add new subparagraph (3) to provide that FLEX Equity Options may only be traded as provided in proposed rules 7155 (FLEX PIP) and 7275 (FLEX Solicitation Auction), and current Rule 7605 (FOO Orders). The Exchange also proposes to provide as new subparagraphs (4) and (5) in Rule 5055(f) (Fungibility of FLEX Equity Options) that: If a Non-FLEX Equity Option series is added intra-day for a component leg(s) of a FLEX Complex Order or FLEX Multi-Leg Order, the holder or writer of a FLEX Equity Option position in the component leg(s) resulting from such FLEX Complex Order or FLEX Multi-Leg Order would be permitted to close its position(s) under the FLEX trading procedures against another closing only FLEX Equity Option position for the balance of the trading day on which the Non-FLEX Equity Option series is added, and; If a Non-FLEX Equity Option series is added for a component leg(s) of a FLEX Complex Order or FLEX Multi-Leg Order on a trading day after the FLEX Complex Order or FLEX Multi-Leg Order position is established, the holder or writer of a FLEX Equity Option position in the component leg(s) resulting from such FLEX Complex Order or FLEX Multi-Leg Order would be required to execute separate FLEX Equity Option and Non-FLEX Equity Option transactions to close its position(s), such that FLEX Equity Option component leg(s) would trade under the FLEX trading procedures and Non-FLEX Equity Option component leg(s) would trade subject to the non-FLEX trading procedures and rules. Lastly, the Exchange proposes to amend Rule 5055(l) to make the Letter of Authorization requirement for transactions in FLEX Equity Options applicable to Order Flow Providers in addition to Floor Brokers. As proposed, Rule 5055(l) will provide: Letter of Authorization. No Floor Broker or Order Flow Provider shall effect any transaction in FLEX Equity Options unless a Letter of Authorization has been issued by a clearing member organization and filed with the Exchange specifically accepting responsibility for the clearance of FLEX Equity Option transactions of the Floor Broker or Order Flow Provider. Self-Regulatory Organizations; Fixed Income Clearing Corporation; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Remove a Requirement That Sponsoring Members Report Certain Events Impacting Their Sponsored Members

1. Purpose FICC is proposing changes to Rule 3A, which describes GSD's sponsored membership service (``Sponsored Service''). Specifically, the proposed rule change would remove the requirement that a Sponsoring Member provide FICC with written notice (i) when it becomes aware that its Sponsored Member is no longer in compliance with applicable requirements of Rule 3A, and (ii) before the effective date of any ``Reportable Event'' applicable to a Sponsored Member. As described below, FICC has implemented changes to the requirements applicable to Sponsored Members and has enhanced its monitoring of Sponsored Members. As a result of such previously implemented changes, FICC believes these reporting requirements for Sponsoring Members are no longer necessary. Overview of Sponsored Service, Sponsored Member Requirements and FICC Monitoring FICC, through GSD, serves as a central counterparty and provides real-time trade matching, clearing, risk management and netting for cash purchases and sales of U.S. Treasury securities as well as repurchase and reverse repurchase transactions involving U.S. Treasury securities (``repos''). GSD's central counterparty services are available directly to entities that are approved to be Netting Members and indirectly to other market participants through its indirect access models--the Sponsored Service or Agent Clearing Service. The Sponsored Service permits Netting Members, approved by FICC as ``Sponsoring Members,'' to sponsor firms, referred to as ``Sponsored Members,'' into GSD membership. The Sponsoring Member is permitted to submit to FICC for comparison, novation and netting certain types of eligible transactions. For operational and administrative purposes, a Sponsored Member appoints its Sponsoring Member to act as processing agent with respect to the Sponsored Member's satisfaction of its securities and funds-only settlement obligations. A Sponsored Member is an Indirect Participant of GSD and the legal counterparty to FICC for any submitted transactions. However, the Sponsoring Member unconditionally guarantees to FICC the Sponsored Member's performance under a Sponsoring Member Guaranty, which guarantees to FICC the payment and performance of a Sponsored Member's obligations to FICC. Therefore, FICC relies on the financial resources of the Sponsoring Member in relying upon the Sponsoring Member Guaranty. FICC recently adopted enhancements to its access models designed to facilitate access to clearance and settlement services of all eligible secondary market transactions in U.S. Treasury securities in accordance with the Securities and Exchange Commission's final rule regarding Standards for Covered Clearing Agencies for U.S. Treasury Securities and Application of the Broker-Dealer Customer Protection Rule With Respect to U.S. Treasury Securities. Among these enhancements, FICC removed the eligibility requirement that Sponsored Members either be ``qualified institutional buyers,'' as such term is defined by Rule 144A under the Securities Act of 1933, or otherwise satisfy the financial requirements of such definition. With this change, Section 3(a) of Rule 3A now provides only that a Person shall be eligible to become a Sponsored Member if it is sponsored into membership by a Sponsoring Member, as provided under the Rules. FICC monitors the risks presented by its Indirect Participants in various ways, consistent with the requirements of Rule 17ad-22(e)(19) under the Act. For example, FICC may request information from direct clearing members periodically through its annual or ad hoc due diligence requests, as required by Section 2(d) of Rule 3A and Section 2 of Rule 3. This monitoring may include the request and review of information related to direct clearing members' Indirect Participants, where applicable, and controls the direct clearing member has in place to monitor and manage the risk presented by those Indirect Participants. FICC also maintains procedures pursuant to which it actively monitors adverse news events impacting Sponsored Members. FICC has recently enhanced these procedures to use Sponsored Members' Legal Entity Identifiers (``LEIs'') in that monitoring. By relying on a Sponsored Member's LEI, rather than its legal name, FICC can continue to identify adverse news events even after a Sponsored Member has changed its name. FICC uses a compliance tool sourced from a third- party vendor to conduct this monitoring. Proposed Changes To Remove Sponsored Member Reporting FICC is proposing to amend Section 2(g) of Rule 3A by removing the requirement that a Sponsoring Member submits written notice to FICC (i) when it becomes aware that a Sponsored Member is no longer in compliance with the requirements of Section 3(a) of Rule 3A, and (ii) prior to the effective date of any Reportable Event applicable to a Sponsored Member. First, the proposal to remove the requirement that FICC be notified when a Sponsoring Member becomes aware of a Sponsored Member is no longer in compliance with the requirements of Section 3(a) of Rule 3A would correct an error in the Rules. FICC has already removed the requirements applicable to Sponsored Members that were in Section 3(a) of Rule 3A. Therefore, this part of the reporting requirement is no longer applicable. The proposed changes would also remove a statement from Section 3(b) of Rule 3A that refers to the requirements that were previously in Section 3(a) of Rule 3A and was also left in the Rules in error. 1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend the Fee Schedule to: (1) increase the per contract fee assessed to Floor Market Makers for Qualified Floor Order (``QFO'') and Complex Qualified Floor Order (``cQFO'') transactions in non-Penny classes that trade against all other origins; and (2) increase the per contract Floor Broker Breakup Credit for QFO and cQFO transactions in non-Penny classes. The Exchange originally filed this proposal on August 31, 2026. On October 27, 2026, the Exchange withdrew SR-SAPPHIRE-2026-35 and refiled this proposal. Background of Fees and Rebates for Transactions on the Trading Floor The Exchange assesses fees for transactions on the Trading Floor based on origin and provides rebates in certain situations. Currently, for Priority Customers and Professional Customers, the Exchange does not assess a per contract fee for QFO and cQFO transactions in SPY/QQQ/IWM, Penny classes (excluding SPY/QQQ/IWM), and non-Penny classes. The Exchange assesses a $0.25 per contract fee for QFO and cQFO transactions in SPY/QQQ/IWM, Penny classes (excluding SPY/ QQQ/IWM), and non-Penny classes for Away Market Maker, Firm, and Broker-Dealer origins. The Exchange does not assess a fee for QFO and cQFO transactions in SPY/QQQ/IWM, Penny classes (excluding SPY/QQQ/ IWM), and non-Penny classes for Firm and Broker-Dealer origins that are facilitating a Priority Customer or Professional Customer order. The Exchange assesses Floor Market Makers a fee of $0.50 per contract for QFO and cQFO transactions in all classes that trade against all other origins. The Exchange provides a rebate of ($0.10) per contract for QFO and cQFO transactions in SPY/QQQ/IWM, Penny classes (excluding SPY/ QQQ/IWM), and non-Penny classes for Floor Broker origins on both the agency and contra sides when that side is billable. The Exchange provides a Floor Broker Breakup Credit of ($0.20) per contract for QFO and cQFO transactions in SPY/QQQ/IWM, Penny classes (excluding SPY/QQQ/ IWM), and non-Penny classes. The Exchange also assesses lower fees for Away Market Maker Facilitation transactions based on the monthly percentage of order volume that is broken up and depending on whether certain volume thresholds are met for each qualifying QFO or cQFO. The Away Market Maker Facilitation rates apply to any Trading Floor transaction where a Member firm Away Market Maker directs a paired order to the Trading Floor, where the agency order is a customer of the affiliated Member firm, and where the contra-side of the transaction is the Away Market Maker of the Member firm. Proposal to Increase the Floor Market Maker Fee for QFO and cQFO Transactions in Non-Penny Classes The Exchange proposes to amend the table of QFO and cQFO fees and rebates in section 1)c)i) of the Fee Schedule to increase the fee assessed to Floor Market Makers for QFO and cQFO transactions in non- Penny classes that trade against all other origins. Currently, the Exchange assesses Floor Market Makers a fee of $0.50 per contract for QFO and cQFO transactions in non-Penny classes that trade against all other origins. The Exchange now proposes to assess Floor Market Makers a fee of $0.94 per contract for QFO and cQFO transactions in non-Penny classes that trade against all other origins. The purpose of this change is for business and competitive reasons. The Exchange believes that even with the proposed increased fee, the Exchange's transaction fees for Floor Market Makers will remain competitive with the fees assessed by other equity options exchanges that offer trading floors for transactions by their market makers in non-penny classes when trading against all other origins. Proposal To Increase the Floor Broker Breakup Credit for QFO and cQFO Transactions in Non-Penny Classes Next, the Exchange proposes to amend the table of QFO and cQFO fees and rebates in section 1)c)i) of the Fee Schedule to increase the per contract Floor Broker Breakup Credit for QFO and cQFO transactions in non-Penny classes. Currently, the Exchange provides a Floor Broker Breakup Credit of ($0.20) per contract for QFO and cQFO transactions in SPY/QQQ/IWM, Penny classes (excluding SPY/QQQ/IWM), and non-Penny classes. The Exchange now proposes to increase the Floor Broker Breakup Credit to ($0.25) per contract for QFO and cQFO transactions in non- Penny classes. The purpose of this change is for business and competitive reasons. The Exchange believes this change may encourage additional Floor Broker liquidity in non-Penny Classes. Additional liquidity in non-Penny classes may benefit all market participants because it will attract additional liquidity to the Exchange by providing more trading opportunities. Further, additional liquidity helps contribute to a robust trading environment on the Exchange's Trading Floor, particularly as it continues to ramp up operations, having launched only a year ago. * * * * * The proposed changes are immediately effective. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act, in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act, in particular, in that it is not designed to permit unfair discrimination among customers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange also believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b)(4) of the Act because it represents an equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among its Members or issuers using its facilities. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Investors Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 11.271 Regarding the Resumption of Trading Following a Level 3 Market-Wide Circuit Breaker Halt

Self-Regulatory Organizations; Investors Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 11.271 Regarding the Resumption of Trading Following a Level 3 Market-Wide Circuit Breaker Halt

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 11.271 (``Trading Halts Due to Extraordinary Market Volatility'') concerning the resumption of trading following a Level 3 market-wide circuit breaker (``MWCB'') halt in connection with the upcoming extension of trading by other national securities exchanges to 23 hours per day, 5 days per week. Although only some exchanges will offer overnight trading, the uniform Level 3 MWCB rules of every exchange are being modified, as explained further below. Background The MWCB mechanism under Rule 11.271 provides an important, automatic mechanism that is invoked to promote stability and investor confidence during a period of significant stress when U.S. securities markets experience extreme broad-based declines. All U.S. equity exchanges and FINRA (collectively, the self-regulatory organizations or ``SROs'') adopted uniform rules relating to the MWCB mechanism in 2012, which are designed to slow the effects of extreme price movement through coordinated trading halts across U.S. securities markets when severe price declines reach levels that may exhaust market liquidity. Currently, market-wide circuit breaker rules provide for trading halts in all U.S. cash equities and equity options markets during a severe market decline as measured by a single-day decline in the S&P 500 Index during Regular Market Hours. Pursuant to Rule 11.271, a market-wide trading halt will be triggered if the S&P 500 Index declines in price by specified percentages from the prior day's closing price of that index. Currently, the triggers are set at three circuit breaker thresholds: 7% (Level 1), 13% (Level 2), and 20% (Level 3). A market decline that triggers a Level 1 or Level 2 halt after 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time and before 3:25 p.m. Eastern Time would halt market-wide trading for 15 minutes, while a similar market decline at or after 3:25 p.m. Eastern Time would not halt market-wide trading. If a Level 3 Market Decline occurs at any time during the trading day, trading in all stocks will halt on the Exchange for the remainder of the trading day, and will resume the following trading day at 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time. Proposal The Exchange now proposes to amend Rule 11.271 to reflect the upcoming extended trading hours, i.e., 23/5 trading, that other exchanges will participate in. When 23/5 trading begins on December 6, 2026, the Exchange's current trading sessions will not change. The Exchange operates three separate trading sessions between 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time and 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time. These are the Pre-Market Session, which operates from 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time to 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time; the Regular Market Session, which operates from 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time; and the Post-Market Session, which operates from 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time to 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time. Consistent with the uniform rules in place across all SROs, current Rule 11.271(b)(2) provides that if a Level 3 MWCB occurs at any time during the trading day, trading in all stocks will halt on the Exchange for the remainder of the trading day. Currently, that means that the earliest that any exchange would re-open trading after a Level 3 MWCB is at 4:00 a.m. Eastern Time the following day, since no SROs are open for trading before 4:00 a.m. Eastern Time. Unless amended, when 23/5 trading is launched, the current rule's reference to halting ``for the remainder of the trading day'' would require SROs participating in 23/5 trading to re-open trading at an earlier time, i.e., 9:00 p.m. Eastern Time on the same calendar day, when those SROs' systems would generally become available for overnight trading. The Exchange does not believe that this is an expected or desired result and is therefore amending this rule in coordination with the other SROs such that trading on any SRO will not resume until 4:00 a.m. Eastern Time or later on the following trading day, consistent with current market practice. This proposed rule change is therefore not intended to make any substantive changes to the MWCB mechanism. Rather, the proposed rule change would preserve the current resumption time following a Level 3 MWCB. To effect this change, the Exchange proposes to delete the language in Rule 11.271(b)(2) that provides that trading in all stocks will halt on the Exchange ``for the remainder of the trading day'' if a Level 3 MWCB occurs at any time during the trading day, and replace it with new language that explicitly provides that trading in all stocks would halt on the Exchange until 4:00 a.m. Eastern Time or later on the following trading day. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the requirements of the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder that are applicable to a national securities exchange, and, in particular, with the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act. Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act in that it is designed to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to, and perfect the mechanism of, a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. The MWCB mechanism described in Rule 11.271 is an important, automatic mechanism that is invoked to promote stability and investor confidence during periods of significant stress when U.S. securities markets experience extreme broad-based declines. Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Definition of Clearing Corporation in its Rules and Make Corresponding Changes Throughout its Rules

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend the definition of Clearing Corporation in its Rules and make corresponding changes throughout its Rules, as well as update Rule 5.2 regarding units of trading. For background, Rule 1.1 currently defines the ``Clearing Corporation and OCC'' as The Options Clearing Corporation. Prior to October 22, OCC was the only clearing corporation registered under Section 17A of the Securities and Exchange Act to clear options listed on a national securities exchange. However, the Securities and Exchange Commission (the ``Commission'') recently approved an application of Cboe Clear US, LLC (``CCUS'') seeking temporary registration as a clearing agency under Section 17A of the Act. Further, it is possible additional entities could register as a clearing agency under the Act to clear listed options. As indicated in a separate Exchange rule filing the Commission recently approved, the Exchange intends to clear certain options through CCUS. This proposed rule change would accommodate the clearing of options listed for trading on the Exchange and cleared by either OCC or CCUS (or any other clearing agencies that become registered under Section 17A of the Act). The proposed rule change amends the definition of Clearing Corporation in Rule 1.1 to mean the clearing agency registered to clear listed options under Section 17A of the Act that is the issuer of and clearing agency for the applicable option or at which a Clearing Trading Permit Holder is a clearing member. The proposed rule change separately defines OCC as The Options Clearing Corporation, as the Exchange retains certain references to OCC with respect to certain options that will continue to be issued and cleared by OCC. Additionally, the proposed Rule change amends the definition of Rules of the Clearing Corporation in Rule 1.1 to mean the governing documents and rules of the Clearing Corporation, and all written interpretations thereof, as they may be in effect from time to time; in other words, the rules of the Clearing Corporation will refer to the governing documents and rules of the applicable registered clearing agency. The proposed rule change amends various other rule provisions to refer to the Clearing Corporation rather than OCC and to otherwise modify those provisions so they contemplate multiple registered clearing agencies (e.g., add that a reference to Clearing Corporation means the ``applicable'' Clearing Corporation or the Clearing Corporation ``that is the issuer of the applicable options''). Pursuant to the proposed definition of Clearing Corporation, these Rules, as well as current Rules that reference Clearing Corporation, will refer to the applicable registered clearing agency in the context of the Rule rather than OCC. The proposed rule change similarly amends Rule 3.61 regarding letters of guarantee and authorization to account for the existence of multiple registered clearing agencies that clear options listed on the Exchange and Clearing TPHs being Clearing Members of more than one of such clearing agencies. First, subparagraph (a)(4) currently provides if the Clearing Corporation restricts the activities of a Clearing TPH or suspends a Clearing TPH as a Clearing Member of the Clearing Corporation, the Exchange may take action as necessary to give effect to the restriction or suspension. For example, if the Clearing Corporation restricts transactions cleared by a clearing Trading Permit Holder that is a Clearing Member of that Clearing Corporation to ``closing only'' transactions, the Exchange may similarly restrict transactions on the Exchange for clearance by that Clearing TPH as a Clearing Member of the Clearing Corporation to ``closing only'' transactions. Similarly, if the Clearing Corporation suspends a Clearing TPH, the Exchange may prevent access and connectivity to the Exchange by the suspended Clearing TPH. The proposed rule change amends this provision so actions the Exchange may take against a Clearing TPH pursuant to this provision are in response to actions taken by the specific Clearing Corporation that took action against the Clearing TPH. While the proposed rule change provides that the Exchange may restrict transactions to closing only in options a Clearing Corporation issues if that Clearing Corporation similarly restricts that Clearing TPH, the proposed rule change does not prevent the Exchange from exercising its authority to impose restrictions on a Clearing TPH provided by other Rules. Further, if the Exchange prevents access and connectivity to the Exchange by a Clearing TPH that is suspended by one Clearing Corporation, that Clearing TPH will not be able to access and connect to the Exchange to participate in transactions in options issued by another Clearing Corporation. If a CTPH is suspended as a Clearing Member by one Clearing Corporation in accordance with rules of that Clearing Corporation, the Exchange believes such action by that Clearing Corporation makes it appropriate for the Exchange to prevent access to the Exchange in all options, even if another Clearing Corporation does not take similar action against that CTPH. Similarly, the proposed rule change amends subparagraphs (a)(5) and (6) to account for the possibility of multiple clearing agencies by providing that the effectiveness of a Clearing TPH's letters of guarantee and authorization is tied to that Clearing TPH's status as a Clearing Member at the Clearing Corporation to which those letters relate. title: IEX to Decommission Single-Channel DEEP+ Market Data Feed
raw_text:
IEX to Decommission Single-Channel DEEP+ Market Data Feed
Category: Market Data and Connectivity; Alert 2026-044
Overview Effective Friday, April 30, 2027, IEX Equities will decommission the single-channel DEEP+ order-by-order depth-of-book market data feed. Channelized DEEP+ will replace the single-channel DEEP+ feed. See IEX Trading Alerts 2026-002 and 2026-017 for more information about Channelized DEEP+. Current Data Subscribers of the single-channel DEEP+ feed must transition to Channelized DEEP+ before the decommission date to continue receiving DEEP+ data. This change does not affect TOPS, DEEP, or Channelized DEEP+. Data Subscribers already receiving Channelized DEEP+ do not need to migrate. Effective immediately, IEX will no longer accept new subscription requests for the single-channel DEEP+ feed. Why is IEX making this change? The new, channelized version is now live and serves as a replacement for single-channel DEEP+. The new version is designed to be more performant, resilient and consistent as it relates to market data delivery measurement. Details Channelization provides for distribution of DEEP+ data across multiple channels. Current single-channel DEEP+ Data Subscribers must move to Channelized DEEP+ to continue receiving DEEP+ data. Anyone who wants to receive the Channelized DEEP+ feed and currently does not have an IEX Data Subscriber Agreement in place will be required to execute an IEX Data Subscriber Agreement prior to receiving access to the Channelized DEEP+ feed. Since Channelized DEEP+ is a replacement for the single-channel version, there are no additional fees required to receive Channelized DEEP+. The option to use Channelized DEEP+ is available regardless of whether the Data Subscriber obtains the data directly from IEX or through a third-party vendor. An existing Data Subscriber wishing to use Channelized DEEP+ will be required to update its Data Request Form (Exhibit A to the IEX Data Subscriber Agreement). No re-execution of the IEX Data Subscriber Agreement will be required. To begin the transition, contact Market Operations. raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; 24X National Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Transaction Fees Applicable to Members of the Exchange

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend the transaction fees applicable to Members of the Exchange. Specifically, the Exchange proposes to increase the fee for executions of non-retail and retail orders that remove liquidity from the 24X Book in all securities traded on the Exchange priced below $1.00 per share (``Removed Sub-Dollar Volume'') from 0.09% of the total dollar value of the transaction to 0.28% of the total dollar value of the transaction. The Exchange proposes to implement the rule change on November 2, 2026. The proposed increased fee for Removed Sub-Dollar Volume transactions are consistent with or lower than the fees charged by other exchanges for similar executions, and are intended to incentivize Members to increase the liquidity-providing orders they submit to the Exchange, which would support price discovery on the Exchange and provide additional liquidity for incoming orders. The proposed rule change does not include different fees depending on the number of orders submitted to, or transactions executed on or through, the Exchange. Accordingly, the fees described above are applicable to all Members, regardless of the overall volume of a Member's trading activities on the Exchange. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the provisions of Section 6(b) of the Act in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(4) of the Act in particular, in that it is designed to provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its Members and other persons using its facilities. Additionally, the Exchange believes that the proposed amended fees are consistent with the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act in that they are designed to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest, and, particularly, are not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange operates in a highly competitive market in which market participants can readily direct order flow to competing venues if they deem fee levels at a particular venue to be excessive or incentives to be insufficient. The Exchange believes that the proposed amended fees reflect a simple and competitive pricing structure designed to incentivize market participants to add aggressively priced displayed liquidity and direct their order flow to the Exchange, which the Exchange believes would promote price discovery and price formation and deepen liquidity that is subject to the Exchange's transparency, regulation, and oversight as an exchange, thereby enhancing market quality to the benefit of all Members and investors. The Commission and the courts have repeatedly expressed their preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. In Regulation NMS, while adopting a series of steps to improve the current market model, the Commission highlighted the importance of market forces in determining prices and self-regulatory organization revenues, and also recognized that current regulation of the market system ``has been remarkably successful in promoting market competition in its broader forms that are most important to investors and listed companies.'' As illustrated in the following table, the Exchange notes that the proposed amended fees are comparable to or lower than those in place on other exchanges: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ Fee for removed Fee for removed Exchange volume <$1.00 (non- volume <$1.00 retail) (retail) ------------------------------------------------------------------------ 24X............................. 0.28% of total 0.28% of total dollar value. dollar value. Cboe EDGX....................... 0.30% of total 0.30% of total dollar value. dollar value. MIAX Pearl...................... 0.20% of total 0.20% of total dollar value. dollar value. MEMX............................ 0.28% of total 0.28% of total dollar value. dollar value. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ The Exchange believes that it is appropriate, reasonable, and consistent with the Act to charge a fee of 0.28% of the total dollar value of Removed Sub-Dollar Volume non-retail and retail transactions because it is comparable to or lower than the fees charged by other exchanges for similar transactions. The Exchange further believes that this fee is equitably allocated and not unfairly discriminatory because it applies equally to all Members, and is designed to facilitate increased activity on the Exchange to the benefit of all Members by providing more trading opportunities and promoting price discovery. In conclusion, the Exchange submits that its proposed amended fee structure satisfies the requirements of Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act for the reasons discussed above in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its Members and other persons using its facilities, does not permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers, and is designed to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system and in general to protect investors and the public interest, particularly as the proposal neither targets nor will it have a disparate impact on any particular category of market participant. raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; Fixed Income Clearing Corporation; Order Instituting Proceedings To Determine Whether To Approve or Disapprove a Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Partial Amendment No. 1, To Establish a Guaranty Fund at the Government Securities Division

I. Introduction On July 24, 2026, Fixed Income Clearing Corporation (``FICC'') filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (``Commission'') the proposed rule change SR-FICC-2026-008 pursuant to Section 19(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (``Exchange Act'') and Rule 19b-4 thereunder to modify FICC's Government Securities Division (``GSD'') Rulebook (``GSD Rules'') to establish a guaranty fund designed to cover losses that may arise due to a Member default or non- default loss event. On August 4, 2026, FICC filed Partial Amendment No. 1 to make clarifications and corrections to the proposed rule change (the proposed rule change, as modified by Partial Amendment No. 1, is hereinafter referred to as the ``Proposed Rule Change''). The Proposed Rule Change was published for public comment in the Federal Register on August 11, 2026. The Commission has received comments regarding the substance of the changes proposed in the Proposed Rule Change. On September 15, 2026, pursuant to Section 19(b)(2) of the Exchange Act, the Commission designated a longer period within which to approve, disapprove, or institute proceedings to determine whether to approve or disapprove the Proposed Rule Change. The Commission is instituting proceedings, pursuant to Section 19(b)(2)(B) of the Exchange Act, to determine whether to approve or disapprove the Proposed Rule Change. II. Summary of the Proposed Rule Change A. Background FICC, through GSD, serves as a central counterparty (``CCP'') and provider of clearance and settlement services for transactions in U.S. government securities, including repurchase and reverse repurchase transactions involving U.S. government securities. FICC manages its credit exposures to its Netting Members through the collection of margin to mitigate potential losses from arising from a Member default. FICC maintains financial resources in the form of its Clearing Fund, which is designed to enable FICC to cover potential losses resulting from the failure of the Member or Member family to which FICC has the largest credit exposure. FICC collects Clearing Fund deposits (i.e., Required Fund Deposits) from its Members using a risk-based margin methodology. Required Fund Deposits operate, individually, as each Member's initial margin, and the aggregate of all such Members' deposits is referred to collectively as the Clearing Fund, which currently operates as GSD's default fund. FICC states that this risk- based methodology enables FICC to identify the risks posed by a Member's unsettled portfolio and to quickly adjust and collect additional deposits as needed to cover those risks. B. Proposed Rule Change FICC proposes to establish a Guaranty Fund for GSD, designed to cover losses that may arise due to a Member default or a non-default loss event and enable FICC to support bankruptcy remote treatment for its Clearing Fund deposits. The Proposed Rule Change includes, among other things: Adopting new GSD Rule 4A (Guaranty Fund) to set forth requirements for the Guaranty Fund, including, among other things, that: (i) FICC performs daily stress testing using historical and hypothetical scenarios for purposes of sizing the Guaranty Fund; (ii) FICC sizes the Guaranty Fund at an amount sufficient to cover the stress test deficiency (i.e., losses observed in daily stress testing over required Clearing Fund deposits) that may arise as a result of the default of the two Netting Member Affiliated Families that would potentially cause the largest aggregate credit exposure for FICC in extreme but plausible market conditions (a ``Cover 2 Standard'' or ``Cover 2 Requirement''); (iii) all deposits to the Guaranty Fund must be made in cash; and (iv) FICC has the authority to resize the Guaranty Fund on an intramonth basis if stress test deficiencies breach certain thresholds. Modifying GSD Rule 4 and the Margin Component Schedule to: (i) support bankruptcy remote treatment for Clearing Fund deposits; (ii) exclude the Clearing Fund from loss mutualization; (iii) provide FICC with the authority to require additional margin deposits from Netting Members if their stress test deficiencies exceed predetermined thresholds in relation to the total Required Fund Deposits of all other Members (excluding such Member or Affiliated Family) or would cause the Guaranty Fund to exceed upper bound parameters established for limiting the resizing of the Guaranty Fund; (iv) clarify that FICC would no longer have the authority to ``borrow'' Clearing Fund deposits of non- defaulting Members to provide liquidity to FICC to meet its settlement obligations; (v) provide FICC with the authority to exchange a Netting Member's Clearing Fund deposit in the form of cash for U.S. Treasury securities to provide liquidity to FICC to meet its settlement obligations; and (vi) eliminate fixed minimum Required Fund Deposit amounts and adjust the associated minimum cash composition requirements accordingly. Relocating the loss allocation rules in Section 7 of GSD Rule 4 to a new GSD Rule 4C (Loss Allocation) and modifying the rules to: (i) incorporate the proposed Guaranty Fund into the loss allocation rules and exclude the Clearing Fund from loss mutualization; (ii) eliminate the concept of Tier One Netting Members and Tier Two Members and exclude CCIT Members and Registered Investment Company Netting Members from loss allocation; (iii) adopt a new five-day ``cooling off period'' for Defaulting Member Events and Declared Non-Default Loss Events (also referred to as an ``Event Period''); and (iv) impose an assessment cap on loss allocation during each cooling-off period equal to two times (or 200 percent of) the Member's Guaranty Fund requirement for each Event Period in lieu of the existing loss allocation rounds system. Make other conforming changes throughout the GSD Rules to reflect the adoption of the Guaranty Fund, as described more fully in the Notice of Filing. III. Clearing Agency's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change The principal purpose of the proposed rule change is to adopt the ICC Procedures for Monitoring Compliance with the Eligible Secondary Market Transaction Submission Requirements (the ``ESMT Procedures''). The ESMT Procedures supplement existing provisions of the ICC U.S. Treasury (``UST'' or ``Treasury'') Clearing Rules (the ``Treasury Rules''). II. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. ICC has prepared summaries, set forth in sections (A), (B), and (C) below, of the most significant aspects of these statements. (A) Clearing Agency's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change (a) Purpose ICC proposes to adopt the ESMT Procedures, which formalize ICC's procedures for monitoring compliance by Treasury Participants (``TPs'') with the requirement to submit Eligible Secondary Market Transactions for clearing, consistent with Securities and Exchange Commission (``SEC'' or the ``Commission'') Rule 17ad-22(e)(18)(iv)(A) and (B). The ESMT Procedures supplement existing provisions of the Treasury Rules, including Chapter 2--Membership, Chapter 3--Clearing of Contracts and Chapter 7--Disciplinary Rules. The ESMT Procedures establish how ICC will monitor, review and enforce TP compliance with Treasury Rule 303. ICC intends to adopt these ESMT Procedures to support the clearing of UST securities through its new Treasury clearing service. ICC proposes to make such changes effective following Commission approval of the proposed rule change. The ESMT Procedures consist of three sections. Section 1 specifies that capitalized terms used but not defined in the ESMT Procedures have the meanings specified in the Treasury Rules, unless otherwise indicated. Section 2 sets out the requirement to submit trades for clearing. As specified in Section 2.1, Treasury Rule 303 requires each TP to submit to ICC or another SEC-registered covered clearing agency for clearing, promptly after execution, all trades in contracts that are eligible for clearing at ICC and are Eligible Secondary Market Transactions to which it is a counterparty. ICC will publish on its website all trades in contracts that are eligible for clearing at ICC pursuant to Chapter 30 of the Treasury Rules. A TP may satisfy this requirement by submitting the trade to ICC or to another SEC-registered covered clearing agency. ICC believes the ESMT Procedures that describe how compliance will be monitored provide TPs with transparency and give ICC a clear, documented process for carrying out its monitoring responsibility. Pursuant to Section 2.2, the ESMT Procedures require TPs to promptly notify ICC in writing within 30 calendar days from the date on which the TP learns that it is no longer in compliance with Treasury Rule 303. The notice must include all relevant facts known at the time, such as the approximate duration of the non-compliance, the time at which the non-compliance was remediated or the anticipated remediation steps and expected timing, and the name and contact information of the TP staff member overseeing the matter. In addition, Section 2.2 of the ESMT Procedures require each TP to annually attest to compliance with Treasury Rule 303 (``Annual Attestation''). ICC will announce the due date to TPs, with the due date being no less than 30 calendar days after the announcement. A senior officer authorized to sign for the TP must sign the Annual Attestation and confirm the TP has effective controls in place to ensure compliance with Treasury Rule 303. In the Annual Attestation, the attesting officer must state that they have read and understand the trade submission requirements set forth in the Treasury Rules and in the ESMT Procedures. The attesting officer must also state that the TP has established, maintains and enforces policies, procedures or other controls reasonably designed to ensure ongoing compliance with Treasury Rule 303, and that those controls are reasonably designed to promptly identify and remediate any non-compliance. Finally, the attesting officer must state that the TP complied with Treasury Rule 303 during the 12 months before the date of the attestation. Self-Regulatory Organizations; Texas Stock Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 17.180 To Permit an Issuer To Elect a Higher Listing Tier for an Exchange Traded Product During a Calendar Year and To Provide for the Related Incremental Listing Fee

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 17.180 to allow an issuer to move an exchange traded product (``ETP'') to a higher listing tier during a calendar year. The proposal would enable an issuer to elect the liquidity support associated with a higher tier without waiting until the following year. The proposed rule change would not alter the annual fee for any tier or require any issuer to upgrade an ETP. Background Rule 17.180 establishes three annual listing fee tiers for ETPs: the Signature Tier at $100,000, the Premier Tier at $55,000, and the Core Tier at $10,000. Each tier has corresponding Minimum Performance Standards and daily stipends under the Exchange's Lead Market Maker (``LMM'') Program, as set forth in the Exchange's Fee Schedule. Under the existing framework, an issuer selects the tier it considers appropriate for an ETP for the current year and may select a different tier for the following year. Rule 17.180 does not expressly address a change of listing tier during the calendar year. The Exchange proposes to add paragraph (b) to permit an issuer to elect a higher tier during the year and to specify the resulting additional fee. Election of a Higher Listing Tier Proposed Rule 17.180(b) would permit an issuer to elect to move an ETP to a higher listing tier during a calendar year. Accordingly, an issuer could move an ETP from the Core Tier to either the Premier Tier or the Signature Tier, or from the Premier Tier to the Signature Tier. An issuer that moves an ETP from the Core Tier to the Premier Tier could subsequently elect to move that ETP to the Signature Tier during the same year. The proposed election would be available only for a move to a higher tier. An issuer could not use this provision to move an ETP to a lower tier during the calendar year, including to reverse an earlier change. Following a change, the higher tier would apply for the remainder of the calendar year unless the issuer elects a further change to a higher tier. The existing annual election framework would continue to permit an issuer to select any available tier, including a lower tier, for the following calendar year. Any change would take effect on a trading day specified in the issuer's written notice to the Exchange and confirmed by the Exchange. The Exchange would coordinate the effective date with the issuer and the assigned LMM so that the applicable tier, performance standards, and stipend treatment change together. Any change would apply prospectively beginning on that date. Incremental Listing Fee For an ETP that moves to a higher tier during a calendar year, the issuer would pay an additional listing fee equal to the difference between the annual fee for the higher tier and the annual fee for the tier immediately preceding the change, prorated based on the number of trading days remaining in that year, including the effective date of the change, divided by the total number of trading days in that year. For example, if an issuer moves an ETP from the Core Tier to the Premier Tier with 125 trading days remaining in the year, including the effective date, in a calendar year with 250 trading days, the additional fee would be $22,500 (($55,000-$10,000) x 125/250). A direct move from the Core Tier to the Signature Tier on the same date would result in an additional fee of $45,000 (($100,000-$10,000) x 125/250). If an ETP is upgraded more than once during the calendar year, each additional fee would be calculated using the annual fee for the tier immediately preceding that upgrade. Application of the LMM Program Beginning on the effective date of an upgrade, the Minimum Performance Standards and daily stipends applicable to the higher tier and the ETP's asset class would apply under the Fee Schedule. The upgrade would not change the standards or stipend amounts specified for any tier or create a separate stipend. An LMM would remain eligible for a daily stipend only to the extent it satisfies the applicable performance conditions. For an ETP upgraded to the Signature Tier, the listing fee credit under Rule 17.180(a)(1)(A) would apply to qualifying instances beginning on the effective date of the upgrade. Such credits would be available for the issuer's listing fees in the following year and would expire if not used during that year. The upgrade would not create Signature Tier credits for periods before its effective date. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act, in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5) requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers as well as Section 6(b)(4) as it is designed to provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its members and other persons using its facilities. The Exchange believes that the incremental fee is reasonable because it uses the existing annual fee difference between the two tiers and charges that difference only for the portion of the year during which the ETP participates in the higher tier. Self-Regulatory Organizations; Investors Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend IEX Rule 3.291 (Influencing or Rewarding Employees of Others; Gratuities), To Conform to the Rules of FINRA for Purposes of an Agreement Between the Exchange and FINRA Pursuant To Rule 17d-2 Under the Act

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend IEX Rule 3.291 (Influencing or Rewarding Employees of Others; Gratuities), to make conforming changes to the Rule such that it remains substantially similar to FINRA Rule 3220. The Exchange notes that this filing is based on a rule change proposal recently submitted by FINRA and approved by the Commission, which amended FINRA Rule 3220 (Influencing or Rewarding Employees of Others). Pursuant to Rule 17d-2 under the Act, the Exchange and FINRA entered into an agreement to allocate regulatory responsibility for common rules (the ``17d-2 Agreement''). The 17d-2 Agreement covers common members of the Exchange and FINRA and allocates to FINRA regulatory responsibility, with respect to common members, for the following: (i) examination of common members of the Exchange and FINRA for compliance with certain federal securities laws, rules and regulations and rules of the Exchange that the Exchange has certified as identical or substantially similar to FINRA rules; (ii) investigation of common members of the Exchange and FINRA for violations of certain federal securities laws, rules or regulations, or Exchange rules that the Exchange has certified as identical or substantially similar to a FINRA rule; and (iii) enforcement of compliance by common members with certain federal securities laws, rules and regulations, and the rules of the Exchange that the Exchange has certified as identical or substantially similar to FINRA rules. The 17d-2 Agreement includes a certification by the Exchange that states that the requirements contained in certain IEX Rules are identical to, or substantially similar to, certain FINRA rules that have been identified as comparable. Included among those rules is Rule 3.291, which IEX previously certified to be identical to, or substantially similar to, FINRA Rule 3220. Currently, Rule 3.291 would not be covered under the 17d-2 Agreement because the FINRA 3220 Filing changed FINRA Rule 3220 such that the FINRA rule is no longer identical, or substantially similar to, FINRA Rule 3220. Rule 3.291 prohibits a Member or person associated with a Member from, directly or indirectly, giving or permitting to be given anything of value, including gratuities, in excess of one hundred dollars per individual per year to any person, principal, proprietor, employee, agent, or representative of another person where such payment or gratuity is in relation to the business of the employer of the recipient of the payment or gratuity. By contrast, the recently amended FINRA Rule 3220 prohibits gifts in excess of $300.00, where the gift or gratuity is in relation to the business of the employer of the recipient. The FINRA 3220 Filing also introduced provisions covering: supervision and recordkeeping requirements; gifts incidental to business entertainment; valuation of gifts; aggregation of gifts; personal gifts; bereavement gifts; de minimis gifts and promotional or commemorative items; donations due to federally declared major disasters; or gifts to a Member's associated persons or individual retail customers. Because of the above-described differences between Rule 3.291 and FINRA Rule 3220, Rule 3.291 currently will not be considered a common rule pursuant to the 17d-2 Agreement. To again harmonize its rules with those of FINRA, the Exchange now proposes to conform the text of Rule 3.291 to FINRA Rule 3220, so that it may be incorporated into the 17d-2 Agreement in its entirety. The Exchange believes that these changes will help to avoid confusion among Members of the Exchange that are also members of FINRA by harmonizing Rule 3.291 with FINRA Rule 3220. The proposed changes to Rule 3.291 are designed to enable the Exchange to incorporate Rule 3.291 into the 17d-2 Agreement, further reducing duplicative regulation of Members that are also members of FINRA. For the avoidance of doubt, Rule 3.291 would apply equally to Exchange-only Members as the Exchange believes it appropriately protects against improprieties, such as conflicts of interest, that might arise when a Member or person associated with a Member gives items of value to an employee of another person, such as an institutional customer, vendor or counterparty with the hope of strengthening the relationship with the customer. First, the Exchange proposes to amend Rule 3.291 to increase the gift limit from $100 to $300 per individual per year. FINRA stated that the current gift limit of $100 has been in place since 1992. FINRA increased the gift limit from $100 to $300 to account for past inflation since 1992 and to account for expected future inflation for approximately ten years, thereby reducing the frequency of future upwards adjustments to account for inflation. Consistent with FINRA's determination, the Exchange believes that a $300 gift limit would continue to permit the exchange of business courtesies while helping to guard against excessiveness, and reasonably reflects changes to purchasing power due to inflation since the gift limit was last raised in 1992 as well as approximately ten years of expected future inflation. Second, the Exchange proposes to add a new paragraph (d) to Rule 3.291 that would authorize FINRA, acting on behalf of the Exchange, to conditionally or unconditionally grant an exemption from any provision of 3.291 for good cause shown, provided that such exemption is consistent with the purpose of the Rule, the protection of investors, and the public interest. Specifically, the Exchange proposes that pursuant to Rule Series 9.600, FINRA staff, for good cause shown after taking into consideration all relevant factors, may conditionally or unconditionally grant an exemption from any provision of this Rule to the extent that such exemption is consistent with the purpose of the Rule, the protection of investors, and the public interest.
