title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq PHLX LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Exchange's Transaction Fees at Equity 7, Section 3
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq PHLX LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend the Exchange's Transaction Fees at Equity 7, Section 3

1. Purpose The purpose of the proposed rule change is to amend the Exchange's transaction fees at PHLX Equity 7, Section 3. The Exchange proposes to streamline its schedule of credits to member organizations providing displayed liquidity on Nasdaq PSX, and to eliminate the supplemental credit to member organizations providing displayed liquidity on Nasdaq PSX . First Change Currently, the Exchange pays a credit to a member organization that provides liquidity on Nasdaq PSX through displayed quotes/orders. This credit currently has four separate tiers. The tiers are not labeled in the rule text, but this filing will refer to them as Tier 1 through Tier 4: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ------------------------------------------------------------------------ Tier 4............................... $0.0033 per share executed for Quotes/Orders entered by a member organization that provides 0.15% or more of total Consolidated Volume during the month. Tier 3............................... $0.0032 per share executed for Quotes/Orders entered by a member organization that provides 0.07% or more of total Consolidated Volume during the month. Tier 2............................... $0.0030 per share executed for Quotes/Orders entered by a member organization that provides 0.05% or more of total Consolidated Volume during the month. Tier 1............................... $0.0020 per share executed for all other Quotes/Orders. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ The Exchange proposes to eliminate Tiers 2, 3, and 4. Therefore, the Exchange would pay a member organization providing displayed liquidity on Nasdaq PSX a credit of $0.0020 per share executed for displayed quotes/orders entered by a member organization--regardless of how much volume the member organization provides during the month. Second Change The Exchange currently pays a supplemental credit to a member organization that provides liquidity on Nasdaq PSX through displayed quotes/orders. This is a supplemental credit of $0.00005 per share executed for displayed quotes/orders entered by a member organization that: (i) provides 0.10% or more of total Consolidated Volume during the prior month; and (ii) provides 0.10% or more of total Consolidated Volume during the month. The Exchange proposes to eliminate this supplemental credit. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act, in general, and furthers the objectives of Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act, in particular, in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among members and issuers and other persons using any facility, and is not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange's proposed changes to its schedule of credits are reasonable in several respects. As a threshold matter, the Exchange is subject to significant competitive forces in the market for equity securities transaction services that constrain its pricing determinations in that market. The fact that this market is competitive has long been recognized by the courts. In NetCoalition v. Securities and Exchange Commission, the D.C. Circuit stated as follows: ``[n]o one disputes that competition for order flow is `fierce.' . . . As the SEC explained, `[i]n the U.S. national market system, buyers and sellers of securities, and the broker-dealers that act as their order-routing agents, have a wide range of choices of where to route orders for execution'; [and] `no exchange can afford to take its market share percentages for granted' because `no exchange possesses a monopoly, regulatory or otherwise, in the execution of order flow from broker dealers'. . . .'' The Commission and the courts have repeatedly expressed their preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. In Regulation NMS, while adopting a series of steps to improve the current market model, the Commission highlighted the importance of market forces in determining prices and SRO revenues and, also, recognized that current regulation of the market system ``has been remarkably successful in promoting market competition in its broader forms that are most important to investors and listed companies.'' Numerous indicia demonstrate the competitive nature of this market. For example, clear substitutes to the Exchange exist in the market for equity security transaction services. The Exchange is only one of several equity venues to which market participants may direct their order flow. Competing equity exchanges offer similar tiered pricing structures to that of the Exchange, including schedules of rebates and fees that apply based upon members achieving certain volume thresholds. Within this environment, market participants can freely and often do shift their order flow among the Exchange and competing venues in response to changes in their respective pricing schedules. As such, the proposal reflects the Exchange's ongoing assessment of how to allocate its limited incentive resources in a competitive market and how to maintain a schedule of credits that is understandable and administrable for member organizations. First Change The Exchange believes that eliminating the three volume-based displayed liquidity credit tiers and retaining the existing $0.0020 per share executed credit for all displayed Quotes/Orders is reasonable because it will streamline the schedule and make the applicable credit easier for member organizations to understand and apply. The Exchange has limited resources to devote to incentive programs, and it is appropriate for the Exchange to periodically reallocate those incentives in a manner that best achieves its overall mix of objectives. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; KalshiEX LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change Relating to Listing Standards for Security Futures Products
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; KalshiEX LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change Relating to Listing Standards for Security Futures Products

1. Purpose Kalshi is registered with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (``CFTC'') as a designated contract market (``DCM'') under the Commodity Exchange Act (``CEA'') and notice-registered with the Commission as a national securities exchange for security futures products pursuant to the notice registration provisions of Section 6(g) of the Act. Under its notice-registration, Kalshi lists as security futures cash-settled contracts that convey exposure to the price of an underlying equity security, have no pre-specified expiration date and are designated as Perpetual SFPs in their respective contract specifications, pursuant to listing standard rules for security futures products that it has adopted under a separate rule filing under Section 19(b)(7) of the Act and Rule 19b-7 thereunder filed on September 18, 2026. In light of anticipated trading interest, Kalshi plans to reduce the time to market for the listing and trading of Perpetual SFPs on certain covered securities following their initial public offering (``IPO''). To effect this plan, Kalshi proposes to adopt certain rule changes to the introductory language in Rule 14.3 and Rules 14.3(c) and 14.3(d) of Chapter 14 of the Kalshi Rulebook. Description of Proposed Rule Change Rule 14.3 of Kalshi's Rulebook sets forth the initial listing eligibility criteria for Underlying Securities of Perpetual SFPs listed on the Exchange. Rule 14.3 requires that an Underlying Security that is common stock satisfy several criteria at the time of initial listing in order to be eligible for a Perpetual SFP on the Exchange, including that the Underlying Security must (i) pursuant to Rule 14.3(a), be registered and listed on a U.S. national securities exchange and must be an ``NMS security'' as defined in Section 11A of the Exchange Act and Rule 600(b) of SEC Regulation NMS, (ii) pursuant to Rule 14.3(b), have a market capitalization of not less than $100,000,000,000 (one hundred billion U.S. dollars), (iii) pursuant to Rule 14.3(c), have an average daily value of transactions (``ADTV'') of not less than $450,000,000 (four hundred and fifty million U.S. dollars) over the six months immediately preceding the New Product Committee's review, except where the Underlying Security has been listed for trading for less than six months, in which case the Underlying Security must have an ADTV of not less than $1,000,000,000 (one billion U.S. dollars) over the prior month, (iv) pursuant to Rule 14.3(d), if the Underlying Security is a ``covered security'' as defined in Section 18(b)(1)(A) of the Securities Act of 1933, have had a closing price of at least $3.00 for the previous five consecutive business days preceding the listing of a Perpetual SFP on such Underlying Security (or a closing price of at least $7.50 for the same period if the Underlying Security is not a ``covered security''), (v) pursuant to Rule 14.3(e), have a public float of not less than 7,000,000 (seven million) shares, (vi) pursuant to Rule 14.3(f), have an estimated deliverable supply in excess of 20,000,000 (twenty million) shares, (vii) pursuant to Rule 14.3(g), have an issuer that is current in all periodic reporting obligations under Sections 13 or 15(d) of the Act, and (viii) pursuant to Rule 14.3(j), have at least 2,000 security holders (whether of record or beneficial). The initial eligibility criterion regarding trading volume history of potential Underlying Securities in Rule 14.3(c) is framed in terms of ADTV over the prior month, so does not contemplate Underlying Securities with exchange-trading histories of less than one month. Accordingly, under the current rule, if an IPO occurs on a given day, the earliest date that the Exchange could list a Perpetual SFP on such security would be one month following such date. The Exchange therefore proposes to amend Rule 14.3(c) to provide that, ``where the Underlying Security has been listed for trading for less than one month, . . . the Underlying Security must have had a trading volume (in all markets in which it is traded) of at least 2,400,000 shares since the Underlying Security's initial public offering day.'' The Exchange also proposes to include a definition of ``initial public offering day'' in the introductory language in Rule 14.3, which would define ``initial public offering day'' of an Underlying Security as ``the first day on which the Underlying Security trades `regular way' on a national securities exchange.'' As proposed, this rule change would permit the Exchange to list a Perpetual SFP on an Underlying Security with a trading volume of 2,400,000 shares since its IPO, regardless of the length of time between the IPO and the New Product Committee's review of the Underlying Security, subject to satisfaction of all other initial eligibility criteria in Rule 14.3, as amended herein. This proposed amendment is consistent with the trading volume criteria adopted by securities options exchanges with respect to the eligibility criteria for underlying securities of securities options, which require such underlying securities to have had a total trading volume of 2,400,000 shares in the preceding twelve months without specifying a monthly ADTV requirement or any minimum lookback period. Additionally, the minimum share price criterion in Rule 14.3(d) requires the market price per share of an underlying covered security to have been at least $3.00 for the previous five consecutive business days preceding the date on which the Exchange commences to list and trade a Perpetual SFP on such Underlying Security (the ``five-day lookback period''). Under the current rule, even assuming adoption of the proposed amendment to Rule 14.3(c) discussed above, if an IPO occurs on a Monday, the earliest date the Exchange could list a Perpetual SFP on the relevant security would be the following Monday, with the market price determined by the closing price over the five-day lookback period from the Monday of the IPO through the following Friday.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq PHLX LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposal To Amend Equity 4 To Remove All References to the CORE FIX Order Entry Protocol
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq PHLX LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposal To Amend Equity 4 To Remove All References to the CORE FIX Order Entry Protocol

1. Purpose In September 2025 the Exchange added CORE FIX to its rulebook in Equity 4, in anticipation of making this new order entry protocol available to Exchange Participants in October of 2025. In December 2025 the Exchange extended the implementation date for CORE FIX to the first quarter of 2026. In March 2026 the Exchange extended the implementation date for CORE FIX to the end of 2026. In spite of its best efforts, the Exchange has been unable to generate interest in CORE FIX among Exchange Participants. Therefore, rather than deploy an order entry protocol that Participants are not even interested in testing, the Exchange proposes to abandon its plans to deploy CORE FIX. This will allow the Exchange to better allocate its technological development resources. The Exchange notes that it will continue to offer all the order entry protocols that are currently available and operative on the Exchange--namely, OUCH, RASH, FLITE, and FIX. The Exchange proposes to eliminate all references to CORE FIX that are currently present in Equity 4. Specifically, these references are found in Rules 3100 (Limit Up-Limit Down Plan and Trading Halts on PSX), 3301A (Order Types), 3301B (Order Attributes), and 3307 (Processing of Orders). 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act, in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act, in particular, in that it is designed to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general to protect investors and the public interest. The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is designed to promote just and equitable principles of trade because it will ensure that the Exchange's rulebook accurately reflects the order entry protocols that are available and operative on the Exchange. Removing references to CORE FIX, which the Exchange will not deploy, will avoid confusion among Participants and other market participants regarding the protocols available for order entry. The proposed rule change will not alter the operation of the Exchange's market, the treatment of orders, or the rights or obligations of Participants; the Exchange will continue to offer the OUCH, RASH, FLITE, and FIX protocols. Accordingly, the proposal will remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and will protect investors and the public interest by providing clear and accurate information concerning the Exchange's order entry protocols. B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule change is not designed to address any competitive issue; instead, its purpose is to ensure that the Exchange's rulebook accurately reflects the protocols that are available and operative on the Exchange. Removing references to CORE FIX will not deprive any Participant of an available order entry protocol, because CORE FIX has not been deployed on the Exchange. Participants will continue to be able to choose among the OUCH, RASH, FLITE, and FIX protocols based on their trading needs. Accordingly, the proposal will not impose any burden on competition, either among Exchange Participants or between the Exchange and other trading venues. C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others No written comments were either solicited or received. III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act and subparagraph (f)(6) of Rule 19b-4 thereunder. At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved. IV. Solicitation of Comments Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods: Electronic Comments Use the Commission's internet comment form (https://www.sec.gov/rules/sro.shtml); or Send an email to [email protected]. Please include file number SR-PHLX-2026-65 on the subject line. Paper Comments Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090. All submissions should refer to file number SR-PHLX-2026-65. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; New York Stock Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rules 7.35 and 7.35A
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; New York Stock Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rules 7.35 and 7.35A

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 7.35 (General) and Rule 7.35A (DMM-Facilitated Core Open and Trading Halt Auctions) to change when the Exchange begins disseminating Auction Imbalance Information for an IPO Auction. Specifically, the Exchange proposes to begin disseminating such information at the later of (A) 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time (``ET''), or (B) the earlier of (i) the time the Designated Market Maker (``DMM'') publishes the first pre-opening indication for the security pursuant to Rule 7.35A(d), or (ii) 10:00 a.m. ET. As discussed below, the Exchange currently begins disseminating Auction Imbalance Information for an IPO Auction at 8:00 a.m. ET, the same time applicable to all other Core Open Auctions, without regard to whether the underwriting syndicate has completed the IPO distribution process. This approach differs from that taken by at least one other national securities exchange, as described below. The Exchange believes that disseminating Auction Imbalance Information before the underwriting syndicate has finalized the distribution may result in information that does not reflect material aspects of the transaction and may therefore be misconstrued by market participants as indicative of the anticipated market for the security. The proposed change would better align the dissemination of Auction Imbalance Information with the liquidity formation process, thereby increasing transparency and reducing the potential for confusion, while preserving 8:00 a.m. ET as the earliest time such information may be disseminated, consistent with all other Core Open Auctions. Background Rule 7.35(c) governs the Exchange's dissemination of Auction Imbalance Information. Rule 7.35(c)(1) provides that Auction Imbalance Information is updated at least every second, unless there is no change to the information. Rule 7.35(c)(2) provides that Auction Imbalance Information is disseminated until the relevant Auction begins. Rule 7.35A(e) governs the timing, content, and pricing of Auction Imbalance Information specifically for the Core Open Auction and Trading Halt Auction facilitated by a DMM. Rule 7.35A(e)(1)(A) currently provides that, for the Core Open Auction, unless a security is halted, the Exchange will begin disseminating Auction Imbalance Information at 8:00 a.m. Rule 7.35A(e)(1)(D) further provides that the Exchange will not disseminate Auction Imbalance Information for the Core Open Auction if there is no ``Opening Reference Price,'' a term defined in Rule 7.35A(a). Rule 7.35A(e)(3) provides that the Imbalance Reference Price used in Auction Imbalance Information for the Core Open Auction is the Opening Reference Price, unless a pre-opening indication has been published, in which case it is the Opening Reference Price bounded by the pre-opening indication prices. Historically, Rule 7.35(c)(3) provided that the Exchange would not disseminate Auction Imbalance Information at all for a security that was an IPO or Direct Listing and had not yet had its IPO Auction or Direct Listing Auction. In April 2020, in connection with the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the Exchange's Trading Floor operations, the Exchange adopted a series of temporary rule changes suspending this restriction so that Auction Imbalance Information would instead be disseminated for an IPO or Direct Listing in the same manner as for any other Core Open Auction. This temporary relief was subsequently extended on several occasions. In November 2020, the Exchange proposed to make this change permanent, which the Commission approved in 2021. As part of that filing, the Exchange deleted former Rule 7.35(c)(3) in its entirety such that an IPO or Direct Listing that had not yet had its IPO Auction or Direct Listing Auction would no longer be excluded from Auction Imbalance Information dissemination, and would instead be included in the same 8:00 a.m. dissemination applicable to Core Open Auctions generally. To enable the underlying calculation to function for a security with no trading history, the Exchange also amended the definition of the reference price used in that calculation to provide that, for an IPO that had not yet had its IPO Auction, the reference price would be deemed to be the security's offering price. The current definition of Opening Reference Price in Rule 7.35A(a) does not include an IPO-specific value. As described further below, the Exchange proposes to add such a value as part of this filing. Proposed Rule Change As noted, the Exchange's current practice of disseminating Auction Imbalance Information for an IPO Auction beginning at 8:00 a.m., i.e., at the same time as for any other Core Open Auction, differs from the approach taken by at least one other national securities exchange. Nasdaq, for example, does not begin disseminating its order imbalance indicator for an initial public offering until the beginning of the ``Display Only Period'' applicable to that security, and the subsequent ``Pre-Launch Period'' does not end until Nasdaq receives notice from the underwriter that the security is ready to trade. In addition, once disseminated, the reference price used in Nasdaq's imbalance indicator for an IPO is the price closest to the issuer's actual initial public offering price. As a result, Nasdaq's imbalance information for an IPO is not disseminated until information reflecting the completion of the underwriting syndicate's process is available. By contrast, because the Exchange currently begins disseminating Auction Imbalance Information for an IPO Auction at 8:00 a.m. ET, that information may be published before the underwriting syndicate has been finalized and before the DMM has issued a pre-opening indication reflecting the results of that process. At that stage, the information available to the Exchange, and therefore reflected in Auction Imbalance Information under the current approach, is limited. DTN2026-28 - Anthropic, PBC Initial Public Offering on Nasdaq Global Select Market
News CategoryAlertMarketsWhat You Need To Know
Data Technical News#2026-028The Nasdaq Stock Market

Anthropic, PBC - Class A common stock is expected to be listed and begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol ANT on November 19, 2026.

Nasdaq requests that market data distributors update their databases to reflect this upcoming listing and display the symbol at their earliest opportunity.

raw_text:
NYSE and representatives of the U.S. military honor Veterans Day with a moment of silence
Markets: NYSE, NYSE AMERICAN EQUITIES, NYSE ARCA EQUITIES, NYSE AMERICAN OPTIONS, NYSE ARCA OPTIONS, NYSE BONDS, FINRA/NYSE TRF, NYSE NATIONAL, NYSE TEXAS; Services: Trading, Post Trade, Market Data
On Wednesday, November 11, 2026, the NYSE and representatives of the U.S. military will observe a one-minute moment of silence at 9:20 a.m. ET to honor military service men and women in recognition of Veterans Day. A single strike of the NYSE Bell at 9:20 a.m. will indicate the start of the moment of silence.

title: MIAX Exchange Group - Options Markets - Enovix Corporation (ENVX) (ENVX2)
raw_text:
MIAX Options — Listing Alert — MIAX Exchange Group - Options Markets - Enovix Corporation (ENVX) (ENVX2)
Listing Alert MIAX Options November 12, 2026 | 11:29 AM MIAX Exchange Group - Options Markets - Enovix Corporation (ENVX) (ENVX2) Enovix Corporation (ENVX) has announced a warrants distribution effective for Friday, November 13, 2026. ENVX2 will be available for trading on the MIAX Options, MIAX Pearl Options and MIAX Sapphire Options Exchanges on Friday, November 13, 2026. ENVX2 will not be available for trading on the MIAX Emerald Options Exchange. No options on the underlying ENVX will be available for trading on Friday, November 13, 2026. All GTC orders resting on the MIAX order books in ENVX will be canceled at the close of business on Thursday, November 12, 2026. ENVX will resume trading on the MIAX Options, MIAX Pearl Options, MIAX Emerald Options and MIAX Sapphire Options Exchanges on Monday, November 16, 2026. Please Note: ENVX2 options will trade on Cloud 4 on the MIAX Options and Cloud 3 on the MIAX Pearl Options Exchanges and on Cloud 2 on the MIAX Sapphire Options Exchange. Market Makers can use the Member Firm Portal (MFP) to manage their option class assignments. ENVX should be used for class assignments in ENVX2 via MFP All LMM and RMM Option Class Assignments must be entered prior to 6:00 PM ET on the business day immediately preceding the effective date. All changes made after 6:00 PM ET on a given day will be effective two trading days later. Additional details about the Enovix Corporation (ENVX) distribution are provided in the attached OCC Memo. Please contact MIAX Listings with any questions at Listings@miaxglobal.com or (609) 897-7308. ENVX Distribution 60190

IEX Options: Corporate Action Handling - Enovix Corporation (ENVX)
Category: Regulatory; Alert 2026-047

ENVX will be disabled for trading on Friday, November 13, 2026. ENVX will be enabled for trading on Monday, November 16, 2026 with the standard deliverable instruments made available for trading. ENVX is in the Penny Interval Program. Please direct your questions to optionsmarketops@iextrading.com .
